item.title: Tribunal says India cannot withdraw from water treaty with Pakistan
item.description:
An international tribunal on Monday ordered India to “observe its obligations” under a treaty with Pakistan on the sharing of the Indus and other rivers, which the New Delhi government sought to suspend.
It also made an order “prohibiting” India from carrying out works at two hydro-electric projects that could breach the 1960 Indus Water Treaty.
The treaty governs the use of water from six rivers, whose headwaters originate in India but flow into Pakistan as part of the Indus basin -- a resource relied on by hundreds of millions.
The Indus cuts through ultra-sensitive demarcation lines between India and Pakistan in contested, Muslim-majority Kashmir -- a Himalayan territory both countries claim in full.
India said in May 2025 that it was suspending its membership of the treaty after accusing Islamabad of backing a deadly attack on tourists on the Indian side of Kashmir. Pakistan denied the charges.
India immediately rejected the Permanent Court of Arbitration’s ruling that it had no grounds to withdraw from the treaty. Pakistan welcomed the tribunal’s ruling.
India’s Water Minister CR Patil said this year that the government would ensure that “not a single drop of water” will flow into Pakistan, which accused India of seeking to “weaponise” the precious resource.
Pakistan has previously said it would consider any attempt to change the flow of cross-border waterways as an “act of war.”
The Permanent Court of Arbitration said in a statement that it had unanimously found that “none of the grounds” put forward by India to suspend the treaty were justified.
It said India’s construction of hydro-electric projects on the Indus and associated rivers had to conform to the 1960 treaty.
“In a unanimous decision, the court found that none of these grounds could justify suspension or termination of the treaty,” said a statement released by the panel.
“Accordingly, the Indus Waters Treaty remains fully in force, and India must observe its obligations under the treaty, including those relating to the design and operation of its hydro-electric projects on the Western Rivers,” it added.

item.title: G20 finance talks open as US seeks to ramp up pressure on Iran
item.description:
Finance leaders from the Group of 20 major economies open talks Monday at a US-hosted gathering, with the Trump administration seeking to escalate economic pressure on Iran amid a renewed exchange of fire with Tehran.
The gathering of G20 finance ministers and central bank governors takes place through Tuesday in the Blue Ridge Mountains city of Asheville, North Carolina.
But the first exchange of attacks for a month between the United States and Iran in the Middle East loomed over the meetings as leaders convene early Monday.
Also clouding the talks are Trump’s tightening of trade barriers and questions on whether the grouping can still work together to address big economic challenges.
Shortly before talks opened, the European Union urged “continued diplomatic efforts” to reach a peace settlement in the Middle East war, which has also seen Tehran virtually block off the Strait of Hormuz.
The waterway is a crucial path of global energy transit, and its closure has caused oil prices to spike.
The G20 comprises 19 nations plus the EU and the African Union. It was established in the wake of the 1997-1998 Asian financial crisis to boost global economic and financial stability.
The EU added that it welcomes efforts at ensuring Iran ceases its “destabilizing activities and engages in peace negotiations with good faith,” including through additional, US-led economic pressure.
It pledged to work with international partners to maintain pressure on Tehran.
US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent skipped last year’s meeting led by South Africa, which has been excluded from the group by the US. Washington holds the rotating presidency this year.
Instead, US officials invited Poland to the table, although it is not a permanent G20 member.
Brazil’s finance minister is shunning the gathering amid tensions with the Trump administration.
A Russian representative is participating, too. A European official speaking on condition of anonymity expressed disapproval that Moscow -- at war with Ukraine since its 2022 invasion -- was not excluded.
Besides promoting economic growth, US priorities this year include dealing with “global imbalances” and sovereign debt challenges, a senior US Treasury official told reporters ahead of talks.
G20 discussions will seek to ensure that economies avoid policies that push excess production and capacity into global markets, the official added.
This echoes criticism of China’s excess industrial capacity, which critics say drives down prices and causes unfair competition.
“Those are difficult conversations to have,” Josh Lipsky of the Atlantic Council told AFP.
He added that the US-Canada trade war weighs on unity among the Group of Seven advanced economies as countries broach tough topics in the wider grouping.
G7 finance ministers are also expected to meet on the margins of the Asheville talks.
Certain reporters from major US newsrooms, including The New York Times and Bloomberg News, were not granted credentials to cover the gathering.
Bloomberg News said the Treasury offered no explanation for rejecting its numerous accreditation requests.
The Times said its economic policy reporter was excluded. Another Times reporter, covering Europe, was allowed access.
A Treasury spokesperson said it plans to welcome nearly 300 media representatives from around a dozen countries.
The official added that access to policymakers during the event comes with “a responsibility to report factual information consistent with established journalistic standards.”
Coverage should not prioritize “clicks, engagement, or sensationalism,” the spokesperson said.
All eyes will be on bilateral meetings on the sidelines of the summit too, where Bessent is set to make direct appeals to counterparts as Washington pushes to isolate Iran economically.
A Treasury official said Bessent will deliver a strong statement to the G20 to urge compliance with US sanctions if they want to continue operating in the dollar-based financial system.
Business leaders will also be present at G20 discussions this year on barriers to investment, innovation and productivity.

item.title: Customs to strictly examine import consignments
item.description:
Customs intelligence units are asked to coordinate examinations of import consignments to avert cumbersome crosscheck and thus reduce port clearance time and cost of business for importers.
The National Board of Revenue (NBR) has issued the order for customs intelligence units to coordinate with the Customs Intelligence and Investigation Directorate (CIID) and the Central Intelligence Cell (CIC) in such work, as businesses often resent overlapping of trade scrutiny.
Customs officials have also been instructed not to seek documents beyond those specified in the Goods Declaration, Assessment and Re-assessment Rules 2024.
They cannot demand manual copies of documents already submitted electronically.
The directives are part of 12 urgent instructions issued by the NBR to customs houses and stations across Bangladesh to ensure revenue security while expediting the clearance of imported goods.
It was a long-pressed demand from the business community to simplify customs process and coordinate investigation processes rather than separately seeking documents from them.
The government's revenue authority has also instructed customs authorities to strengthen risk-based examination, eliminate unnecessary procedures and avoid multiple physical examinations of the same consignment unless a confirmed risk does exist.
The directions on dos and don'ts, issued on August 30, call for regular updating of the Asycuda World System selectivity criteria so that consignments can be selected for examination based on revenue risks.
"Findings from physical examinations should also be used to improve future risk-selection criteria," said the latest order on external-trade front.
The NBR has also directed officials to avoid unnecessary manual registers and data recording and not to forward files of non-risky consignments to higher authorities unless there are specific instructions from the revenue board.
Responsible officers must regularly monitor unstuffing activities and gate verification at sea, land and air ports, it said.
All unnecessary steps in the assessment and clearance process should be eliminated, according to the directives.
To expedite the release of imported goods, customs authorities have been asked to issue notices to importers and clearing and forwarding (C&F) agents and take legal action where necessary.
The NBR has also ordered customs authorities to complete auction procedures for stuck-up goods swiftly.
The notification, signed by Second Secretary (Customs: Policy) Rezaul Karim, was circulated to major Customs, Excise and VAT Commissionerates for immediate implementation.

item.title: Savings tools: Premature encashment cuts profit; lack of TIN increases tax
item.description:
When thinking of safe investments, National Savings Certificates ( Sanchayapatra ) are the top choice for many.
For middle-income and fixed-income individuals in particular, it serves as both a means of saving and a source of regular income.
Many also invest with future needs in mind, such as education, medical treatment, or household emergencies.
However, without a clear understanding of maturity periods, profit rules, taxation, and personal financial needs prior to purchasing, investors may fail to earn desired returns—or even face financial losses when attempting to withdraw funds during emergencies.
Five mistakes to avoid before buying savings certificates
It is unwise to invest funds into long-term savings certificates if they might be needed soon for emergency funds, medical care, or urgent expenses. Capital is generally locked in for several years. Breaking certificates before maturity means forfeiting expected profit rates. If there is a chance you will need the money within a few months, it is best not to invest those funds in savings certificates.
Profit rates and governing rules vary depending on the total investment amount. Before committing large sums, it is essential to verify current rules, overall investment limits, and applicable profit tiers. If planning to invest under the names of multiple family members, consider the source of funds, legal ownership, and tax regulations separately for each individual. Investments should never be made in someone else’s name solely to evade taxes.
Withholding tax applies to profits earned from savings certificates. Lacking proper clarity on Tax Identification Numbers (TIN), tax return filings, and related tax rules may lead to higher tax deductions from your profit than expected. Before purchasing, it is advisable to check your tax status and applicable withholding tax rates with relevant authorities or a tax professional.
Not all savings certificate schemes distribute profits in the same manner. Some investors require regular monthly income, while others prefer receiving a lump sum upon maturity. For instance, Family Savings Certificates offer regular profit payouts, while others pay out quarterly. Rather than looking solely at the highest profit rate, select a scheme based on your specific financial needs and cash flow requirements.
Putting all future savings exclusively into savings certificates is not a risk-free strategy. It is far better to create separate plans for short-, medium-, and long-term horizons aligned with your financial needs. Alongside setting aside easily accessible funds for emergency expenses, plan for long-term investments. This reduces the risk of having to break long-term investments prematurely when sudden cash needs arise.
Before buying savings certificates
Before investing, it is essential to learn about the current profit rates, tenure, investment limits, tax rules, and early encashment penalties for the specific savings certificate.
Additionally, decisions should be made taking into account your personal financial goals and future cash flow requirements.
Rather than investing all savings into a single sector simply because it feels safe, investing based on a comprehensive financial plan is far more important.
Investment Scenario / Factor
Key Risk / Impact
Recommended Strategy
Premature Encashment
Reduced Profit Yield: Breaking certificates before maturity forfeits standard yields; profits are recalculated at lower penalty rates.
Keep emergency reserves in liquid bank accounts; only lock funds intended for full tenure.
Missing TIN / Tax Return
Higher Tax Deduction: Higher withholding tax rates are levied on profit distributions if TIN/tax return proof is not updated.
Obtain a valid TIN and file annual income tax returns to qualify for lower withholding tax rates.
Exceeding Investment Slabs
Lower Effective Returns: Crossing specific investment thresholds (slabs) drops the applicable profit rate tier.
Review individual and joint holding limits across all schemes prior to purchasing.
Mismatched Payout Structure
Cash Flow Distress: Choosing maturity-based growth schemes when regular cash is required causes liquidity strains.
Align scheme choice (e.g., Family Savings Certificate for monthly payouts vs. 3-Month Profit Certificate) with cash flow needs.
Single-Asset Allocation
Liquidity Lockup: Concentrating 100% of wealth into long-term certificates leaves no buffer for unexpected costs.
Diversify into a mix of short-term liquid funds, medium-term deposits, and long-term certificates.
Government savings certificates in Bangladesh offer tiered returns where maximum yields are unlocked only upon reaching full maturity (e.g., 3 or 5 years).
Encashment within the first year often yields minimal to zero profit, while early withdrawal in subsequent years slashes the rate retroactively.
Having a Tax Identification Number (TIN) and filing proof of income tax returns directly protects your investment yield by preventing maximum source tax deductions (e.g., reducing withholding tax rates from higher penalty brackets down to standard rates).

Elections loom, yet administrators being installed in Union Parishads
item.description:
• Number of Union Parishads in the country: 4,588.

  • Number of eligible unions for election: 311.

  • Elections cannot be held in 4,237 unions as their tenures have not expired. Cases are ongoing in 40 unions.

The government is planning to start holding Union Parishad (UP) elections within this year, and the election commission (EC) is preparing accordingly, with the schedule likely to be announced in September. However, the government is currently appointing administrators to the Union Parishads.

According to Ministry of Local Government sources, administrators have been appointed to at least 38 Union Parishads over the past two months. Among these, 31 are old unions and seven are newly formed.

In some places, government officials have been appointed as administrators, while in others, leaders of the ruling BNP (Bangladesh Nationalist Party) have been placed in these posts. Party leaders have also been appointed as Union Parishad members.

Sources in the Ministry of Local Government indicated that the process of appointing administrators to more Union Parishads is currently underway.

The Ministry of Local Government reasons that the government made this decision to keep public services running smoothly. There is no legal bar to appointing administrators under the law.

State Minister for Local Government Mir Shahe Alam told newspersons at the Secretariat on 17 July that elections to five tiers of local government will be held within this year.

When asked by Prothom Alo why administrators were being appointed under such circumstances, he said the appointments have no relation to the elections and the Union Parishad elections will indeed be held within this year.

When asked why party affiliates are being appointed as administrators to Union Parishads, the state minister said the list of administrators is sent to the ministry from the deputy commissioner's office. It only contains individual names, so there is no opportunity to know who is a government official or a political party leader.

The number of Union Parishads in the country is 4,588. According to data from the Ministry of Local Government, as of 30 July, the number of election-eligible unions was 311. Elections cannot be held in 4,237 unions as their tenures have not expired, and lawsuits are ongoing in 40.

Following the fall of the Awami League government in the July mass uprising on 5 August 2024, many Union Parishad chairmen went into hiding. During the tenure of the interim government, administrators were appointed from among government officials in many places. However, no party affiliates were appointed at that time.

The BNP government has now appointed party affiliates as administrators in several Union Parishads. Sources say local BNP leaders are trying to place party affiliates as administrators in more unions.

Earlier in July, the government made one-year contractual appointments of BNP leaders to top posts in 11 government institutions. BNP leaders have also been appointed as administrators in 11 city corporations, 63 district councils and 8 urban development authorities.

Party leaders as UP administrators

According to sources in the Ministry of Local Government, Faruque Hossain Khokon was given the responsibility of administrator in Mokamia Union of Betagi upazila in Barguna last month. He is the joint convener of Betagi Upazila BNP.

In the Baushia Union Parishad of Gazaria upazila in Munshiganj, Ebadul Haque was appointed as the new administrator. He was the former joint secretary of the upazila Jubo Dal and the member for Ward No. 3 of Baushia Union, where he had previously served as a member.

In Rupganj Union Parishad of Narayanganj, BNP leader Md. Noor Nabi Bhuiyan was appointed as administrator on 19 July. Concurrently, the Local Government Division appointed 12 BNP leaders and activists of various levels as members of the council.

Fazlur Rahman Bhuiyan was appointed as the administrator of Barishal Union Parishad in Akhaura upazila of Brahmanbaria. He is a member of the Brahmanbaria district unit BNP.

Comprising both newly formed and old unions, out of the 38 Union Parishads where administrators were appointed in the past two months, 19 are in Barishal district, representing the highest number.

Sources said that after the tenures of the Union Parishads in Bakerganj, Muladi, and Wazirpur upazilas of Barishal ended, multiple meetings were held regarding appointing BNP leaders as administrators. However, no consensus was reached on who would be selected.

Abul Hossain Khan, Member of Parliament for the Barishal-6 Bakerganj constituency, told Prothom Alo that many leaders want to become Union Parishad administrators.

"If we give it to one, another gets unhappy, which is why no one was appointed. To avoid controversy, administrators are being appointed from among government officials," he said.

The Local Government (Union Parishad) Act states that an administrator will be appointed for a single term of 120 days, though the government can extend the term. If the government wishes, it can run the Union Parishads through administrators without holding elections.

Badiul Alam Majumdar, Secretary of Shushashoner Jonno Nagorik (SHUJAN) told Prothom Alo that if elections are held soon, there is no need to appoint administrators for a short period.

"It is necessary to stop appointing party affiliates to government posts. The government should hold elections as soon as possible. If administrators are appointed instead of holding elections, many may begin to suspect that elections might not be held in all unions," he said.

item.title: Rizvi: Gas supply to normalize by September second week
item.description:
BNP Acting Secretary General Ruhul Kabir Rizvi on Tuesday said normal gas supply across the country is expected to be restored by the first or second week of September.
He made the comments while talking to reporters after paying homage and offering prayers at the graves of BNP founder and late president Ziaur Rahman and former prime minister Khaleda Zia at Sher-e-Bangla Nagar in Dhaka on Tuesday morning.
Rizvi said Bangladesh has also been affected by the ongoing global energy crisis, particularly due to the US-Iran war and disruptions to shipping through the Strait of Hormuz.
“This is a global crisis. Ships cannot come through the Strait of Hormuz because of the US-Iran war and fuel supplies are being disrupted. When one or two ships tried to come, bombs were dropped there,” he said.
He said Prime Minister Tarique Rahman is taking measures to address the energy crisis, allocating Tk40,000 crore from the budget for the energy and power sector to resolve the gas shortage.
Referring to the technical problems at the Floating Storage and Regasification Unit (FSRU) in Maheshkhali, Rizvi said repairs have already been completed and regasification has begun.
“Regasification has now started. Normal gas supply will be ensured by the first or second week of September, and electricity will also be available. We are already seeing some indications of that,” he said.
Speaking about BNP’s founding anniversary, Rizvi said the party believes in politics based on fulfilling its commitments to people.
He said BNP has come to power through a free and fair election and Prime Minister Tarique Rahman has been working tirelessly, day and night, to fulfil the pledges made to the people after taking office.
On the challenges facing the party and government, Rizvi said there are various challenges, conspiracies and plots, but Tarique Rahman is leading the government while confronting them.
“If there were no challenges, there would be no credit in overcoming them and achieving something good,” he said.
Rizvi said the government is also working to implement BNP’s commitments, including the Farmers Card, Family Card and allowances for imams and muezzins.
Asked about the apparent overlap between the party and the government, as BNP is a political party while the government is a separate entity, Rizvi termed the question an “ambiguous term.”
“The people voted for the party, and the party formed the government. The ministers in the government are BNP leaders. Most of them are BNP leaders. So when the people voted for and elected the party, its members will naturally run the government,” he said.
He said BNP had repeatedly made it clear that its leaders and activists, from grassroots members to the national level, were part of the government’s broader effort.
“Our leaders and activists will properly inform the people about all government programmes being implemented for public welfare and in the public interest. There is no contradiction in this,” Rizvi said.
He stressed that the party and government remain separate entities, but the responsibility of running the government lies with BNP and its leaders.

item.title: 1,000 Rohingya to receive skills training under China-backed program
item.description:
A skills development program for 1,000 Rohingya has been launched at Camp 11 in Ukhiya, Cox’s Bazar, with support from the Embassy of the People’s Republic of China in Bangladesh.
National humanitarian development organization Impact Initiative inaugurated the program, titled “Sustainable Opportunities for Livelihoods, Advancement and Resilience (SOLAR),” at the Multipurpose Building of Rohingya Camp 11 on Tuesday.
Md Shariful Islam, deputy secretary and Camp-in-Charge of Camp 11, attended the inauguration as the chief guest, while Impact Initiative Chief Executive Officer Md Enayet Hossain chaired the event.
Under the SOLAR initiative, 325 participants will receive practical, market-oriented technical training in tailoring and dressmaking, block printing and batik, mobile phone servicing, gas burner repair and climate-smart agriculture.
Another 675 participants will receive soft-skills training focused on communication, teamwork, problem-solving, workplace behavior and other essential life and employability skills.
Speaking at the inauguration, Shariful Islam said skills development and practical livelihood training could play an important role in strengthening the capacity and self-reliance of the Rohingya community.
“Initiatives such as SOLAR will help participants develop practical skills and prepare themselves for future livelihood opportunities,” he said.
Enayet Hossain said Impact Initiative was creating opportunities for the Rohingya community to develop practical and market-relevant skills with support from the Chinese Embassy.
“Through the SOLAR initiative, we aim to strengthen their capacity, resilience and prospects for sustainable livelihoods,” he said.
The initiative aims to complement humanitarian assistance with skills development and livelihood-focused interventions, helping Rohingya community members build practical capacities and improve their prospects for self-reliance amid prolonged displacement.
With support from the Chinese Embassy and implementation by Impact Initiative, the program is expected to expand skills and livelihood opportunities for Rohingya community members in the camp.
